name: Omelet Soufflé
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Break six eggs into separate cups
Beat four of the yolks, mix with them one teaspoonful of flour, three tablespoonfuls of powdered sugar, very little salt
Flavor with extract lemon or any other of the flavors that may be preferred
Whisk the whites of six eggs to a firm froth
Mix them lightly with the yolks
Pour the mixture into a greased pan or dish
When well-risen and lightly browned on the top, it is done
Roll out in warm dish, sift pulverized sugar over, and send to table

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Break six eggs into separate cups
2. Beat four of the yolks, mix with them one teaspoonful of flour, three tablespoonfuls of powdered sugar, very little salt
3. Flavor with extract lemon or any other of the flavors that may be preferred
4. Whisk the whites of six eggs to a firm froth
5. Mix them lightly with the yolks
6. Pour the mixture into a greased pan or dish
7. Bake in a quick oven
8. When well-risen and lightly browned on the top, it is done
9. Roll out in warm dish, sift pulverized sugar over, and send to table
